title: What the prescription monitoring statute covers, and its 24-hour submission limit
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A(a)(1) the department SHALL ESTABLISH AND MAINTAIN AN ELECTRONIC SYSTEM TO MONITOR the prescribing and dispensing of ALL SCHEDULE II TO V, INCLUSIVE, CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES AND CERTAIN ADDITIONAL DRUGS by all professionals licensed to prescribe or dispense such substances; for the purposes of s. 24A, 'additional drugs' means SUBSTANCES DETERMINED BY THE DEPARTMENT TO CARRY A BONA FIDE POTENTIAL FOR ABUSE. 105 CMR 700.001 defines an Additional Drug as A CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE IN SCHEDULE VI determined by the Department to carry a bona fide potential for abuse. Under s. 24A(b) the requirements of s. 24A SHALL NOT APPLY TO THE DISPENSING OF CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES TO INPATIENTS IN A HOSPITAL. Under s. 24A(c) the department shall promulgate regulations including (1) a requirement that each pharmacy that delivers a schedule II to V, inclusive, controlled substance or a substance classified as an additional drug by the department to the ultimate user shall submit to the department, by electronic means, information regarding each prescription dispensed for a drug included under subsection (a); and (2) a requirement that each pharmacy COLLECTS AND REPORTS, for each such prescription, A CUSTOMER IDENTIFICATION NUMBER and other information associated with it, as specified by the department. Each pharmacy shall submit the information in accordance with transmission methods and frequency requirements promulgated by the department; PROVIDED, HOWEVER, THAT THE INFORMATION SHALL BE SUBMITTED AT LEAST ONCE EVERY 24 HOURS. The department may issue a waiver to a pharmacy that is unable to submit prescription information by electronic means, permitting submission by other means promulgated by the department, provided that all information required by the section is submitted in that alternative format.
exam_relevance: Tests what brings a dispensing within the monitoring program -- a Schedule II through V controlled substance, or a drug the department has determined to be an additional drug -- and that the statute sets a 24-hour submission limit alongside the transmission rule in the department's own regulation.

numeric_facts.fact: Maximum interval between a pharmacy's submissions of prescription monitoring information
numeric_facts.conditions: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A(c): the information shall be submitted at least once every 24 hours, in addition to the transmission methods and frequency requirements the department promulgates

exceptions: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A(b): the requirements of s. 24A do not apply to the dispensing of controlled substances to inpatients in a hospital.
The department may issue a waiver to a pharmacy unable to submit prescription information by electronic means, provided all required information is submitted in the alternative format.
common_confusions: Taking the department regulation's transmission deadline as the whole of the timing rule, when the statute also requires submission at least once every 24 hours.
Assuming a drug must be federally scheduled to be monitored, when the statute reaches additional drugs the department determines to carry a bona fide potential for abuse.
Assuming every Schedule VI drug is monitored, when among Schedule VI drugs the statute reaches those the department has determined to be additional drugs.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A(a)(1), (b) and (c) read in the current text on malegislature.gov, and the definition of Additional Drug in 105 CMR 700.001 read in the official publication on mass.gov, both on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
